title: The Radian Circle
blurb: A radian is the angle where the arc equals the radius. Drag the point through the sixteen principal angles and watch it measured both ways.

title: Circle → Wave → Fourier → Schrödinger
blurb: One rotating point generates every sine wave, builds arbitrary signals as a Fourier series, and carries a quantum state's phase through time.

title: e, i, and the Long Detour into Quantum Mechanics
blurb: Compound interest and an unsolved cubic gave us e and i — four centuries later they turned out to be the native language of quantum theory.

title: The Ubiquity of Pi
blurb: Pi begins as circumference over diameter, then surfaces in coin flips, factorials, needle drops, and the floor of quantum uncertainty.

title: Feynman's Rotating Clocks
blurb: Feynman explained quantum electrodynamics with spinning arrows: sum a clock hand for every path, and its length gives the probability.

title: The Logarithmic Spiral
blurb: Give e^(iθ) a real exponent and the turning point starts to grow. One constant sets how tightly it winds — the same equiangular curve behind shells, galaxies, and sunflower heads.

title: Epicycles
blurb: Chain enough rotating circles, each spinning at its own steady rate, and their tip traces any shape at all — a square wave, a star, a signature. Fourier, drawn.
